beats.narration_text: Bonjour — this is Liam, in for Komal. A brand used to keep its personality in a PDF. Now it can keep a character that answers. Today: what an AI brand persona actually is, why houses need one now, and one beauty house that already let the brand talk.

beats.narration_text: Start with names, because the industry blurs them on purpose. Brand personality is the adjective page: bold, warm, exclusive. A campaign face is a look you can mint — we already drew that line. An AI brand persona is different: a runnable character with a job, a never-say list, and proof it always cites. Those are not synonyms.

beats.narration_text: Why this is useful now. Volume: every channel talks, and a house cannot staff all of them at two in the morning. Consistency: a generic model defaults to the same helpful voice as every other brand. Test: you can run a draft through the persona before it ships, and catch costume copy.

beats.narration_text: Not every file is a persona. Adjectives without a never-say list will drift. A generated face is not a voice. If the model can say anything, it is not the house — it is a costume.

beats.narration_text: Worked example. L'Oréal showed Beauty Genius at C.E.S. 2024: a branded advisor that diagnoses, recommends, and stays inside the house's products. Not a generic chatbot. A persona with a catalog and a job. That is why brands are building these now — the customer is already talking to a model. The question is whose voice answers.

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Personality is a page. A face is inventory. A persona is a character that can answer. L'Oréal's Beauty Genius is the worked example: the house, on duty. Design judgment: if it has no never-say list, it is not a persona.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude with a brand you actually know. Write the persona file: (1) who it is and who it is for, (2) five things it never says, (3) three proof points it always cites. Then score three live posts: on-voice or costume. Run it before the next campaign meeting.
